'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[ISIL insurgency in Iraq (2017–present)|ISIL insurgency in Iraq]]
**[[July 2021 Baghdad bombing]]
***A [[Suicide bombing|suicide bomber]] blows himself up at a market in [[Sadr City]], [[Baghdad]], [[Iraq]], killing at least 35 people and wounding 50 others. [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] claims responsibility for the attack. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/19/iraq-roadside-bomb-kills-10-in-baghdad (Al Jazeera English)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/two-killed-13-wounded-explosion-iraqs-sadr-city-sources-2021-07-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[Communal conflicts in Nigeria]]
**[[Bandit]]s in Nigeria's [[Zamfara State]] shoot down an [[Alpha Jet]] of the [[Nigerian Air Force]]. The pilot ejected and survived. [https://news.yahoo.com/nigerian-fighter-jet-shot-down-140431602.html (AFP via Yahoo News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*American [[ice cream]] company [[Ben & Jerry's]] announces that they will stop selling their products in areas of the [[Palestinian territories]] that are controlled by [[Israel]], saying that continuing to do this is "inconsistent with our values". In the same statement, the company said that they will continue to sell within Israel proper. The [[Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions]] movement applauded the decision, while [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Naftali Bennett]] and [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Israel)|Minister for Foreign Affairs]] [[Yair Lapid]] harshly criticized it. [https://www.npr.org/2021/07/19/1018039737/ben-jerrys-says-it-will-stop-ice-cream-sales-in-occupied-territories (NPR)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a record 231 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 18,125. [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2021/07/19/daily-covid-deaths-hit-record-231-in-bangladesh-as-toll-tops-18-000 (''Dhaka Tribune'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 1,338 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 74,920. [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5649120/1338-orang-meninggal-angka-kematian-covid-19-hari-ini-pecah-rekor (detikNews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] imposes a nationwide ban on private gatherings of more than four people in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19 cases. The ban is in effect until August 1 with some exceptions. [http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20210718000190 (''The Korea Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record for the fourth consecutive day of 11,784 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 415,170. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2151171/record-11-784-new-covid-cases-81-deaths-reported-monday (''Bangkok Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] imposes "Directive 16", the most stringent [[social distancing]] measures so far, in 16 [[Provinces of Vietnam|provinces]] for the next two weeks, amid an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://e.vnexpress.net/news/news/16-southern-localities-to-begin-two-weeks-of-strict-social-distancing-4326336.html (VNExpress)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] begins to implement a [[Immunity passport|EU Digital COVID Certificate]] and eases non-essential international travel restrictions for those who have been fully [[COVID-19 vaccination in the Republic of Ireland|vaccinated]], tested negative, or recovered from COVID-19. [https://www.rte.ie/news/business/2021/0718/1235888-travel-rules-changes/ (RTÉ)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Italy]]
*****The number of population fully vaccinated against COVID-19 in [[Italy]] reaches 27.1 million, or 50% of its total population. [https://www.thelocal.it/20210719/over-half-of-italy-is-now-fully-vaccinated-against-covid-19/ (''The Local Italy'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] announces that half of the population has been fully [[vaccinate]]d, the third EU nation to do so after [[Malta]] and [[Hungary]]. [https://www.elmundo.es/ciencia-y-salud/salud/2021/07/19/60f5a876fdddffde948b45cf.html (''El Mundo'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]]
*****Most legal restrictions on social contact are ended in [[England]]. [[Face covering]]s in indoor public places are no longer required by law, though they are still recommended in some settings. There are no more limits on how many people can attend events, nightclubs can reopen and table service will not be necessary in pubs and restaurants. People working from home as a result of the [[pandemic]] are formally encouraged to return to their workplace. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-57882029 (BBC News)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]]
*****Restrictions are also being eased across [[Scotland]] to level zero. Unlike in England, face coverings are still mandatory in indoor public places and on public transport. The change also means that four households can meet indoors at home, up to 10 households can meet in a pub or restaurant, up to 15 households can meet outdoors and up to 200 people can attend a wedding or funeral. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-57878745 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Texas]]
****[[Texas]] reports their first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Lambda variant|Lambda variant]] of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]], which was first detected in [[Peru]]. [https://www.newsweek.com/lambda-covid-variant-detected-texas-hospital-1611359 (Newsweek)]
***[[Fox News]] host [[Sean Hannity]] urges viewers to take the threat of [[COVID-19]] seriously, as well as urging viewers to receive the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://people.com/politics/sean-hannity-urges-viewers-get-covid-vaccine/ (People.com)]
*The [[Ethiopian Broadcasting Corporation]] announces the second filling of the controversial [[Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam]] is complete. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/19/ethiopia-says-second-filling-of-renaissance-dam-complete (Al Jazeera)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Afghanistan–Pakistan relations]]
**[[Afghanistan]] withdraws all of its senior diplomats from [[Pakistan]] after the abduction and alleged torture of the [[ambassador]]'s daughter in [[Islamabad]]. Pakistan calls [[Kabul]]'s decision "regrettable" and says that they should reconsider. [https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/afghanistan-pulls-diplomats-out-of-pakistan-after-ambassadors-daughter-attacked-jgm005m7b (''The Times'')]
*[[Georgia–European Union relations]], [[Moldova–European Union relations]], [[Ukraine–European Union relations]]
**[[President of Moldova|Moldovan President]] [[Maia Sandu]], [[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[Volodymyr Zelensky]], and [[President of Georgia|Georgian President]] [[Salome Zourabichvili]] announce in a joint statement their intentions to have their respective countries pursue closer relations with the [[European Union]], effectively rebuking [[Russia]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/georgia-moldova-ukraine-european-union-charles-michel-russia-batumi-conference/ (''Politico'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*Two United States citizens are convicted and sentenced in [[Japan]] for aiding former [[CEO]] of [[Nissan]], [[Carlos Ghosn]], in his escape from Japan to [[Lebanon]] in December 2019. Former [[U.S. Special Forces]] Michael Taylor is sentenced to 2 years' imprisonment while his son receives a 20 months' sentence. [https://www.dw.com/en/japan-court-jails-us-duo-over-ghosn-escape/a-58311408 (DW)]
*[[Morocco|Moroccan]] citizen [[Abdul Latif Nasir]] becomes the first prisoner held at the [[Guantanamo Bay detention camp]] to be released by the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]], as part of the process to reduce the camp's population and eventually close it. Nasir was cleared for release by the [[Periodic Review Board]] in July 2016, but was blocked by the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/19/us-biden-administration-transfers-first-detainee-from-guantanamo (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Peruvian general election]]
**[[Keiko Fujimori]] of the [[right-wing]] [[Popular Force]] (FP) [[Concession (politics)|concedes]] defeat to [[left-wing politics|left-wing]] candidate [[Pedro Castillo]], but accuses him of winning through "illegitimate" means. The accusation comes as the [[National Jury of Elections]] says that it will announce the winner later this week, and dismissed five challenges to the results brought last week by the FP party. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-07-19/perus-fujimori-admits-defeat-in-presidential-election-lashes-out-at-socialist-rival (''U.S. News'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peru-electoral-authority-cusp-confirming-new-president-scraps-last-fujimori-2021-07-19/ (Reuters)]
**The National Jury of Elections confirms Castillo as the winner of the election, thereby making him president-elect. He is expected to be sworn-in as [[President of Peru]] on July 28. [https://en.mercopress.com/2021/07/20/castillo-to-be-peru-s-next-president-after-all (''Mercopress'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Project Pegasus revelations]]
**A consortium of journalists led by [[Non-governmental organization|NGOs]] [[Forbidden Stories]] and [[Amnesty International]] reveal [[Pegasus (spyware)#Discovery of widespread use (2021)|widespread spying abuses on journalists, political opposition, businesspeople, human rights activists and others]] by various governments under the guise of fighting crime or [[terrorism]]. The NGOs accessed a list of over 50,000 individuals targeted by Israeli security and spying software company [[NSO Group]] and its customers within 50 countries. [https://www.theguardian.com/news/series/pegasus-project (''The Guardian'')] [https://forbiddenstories.org/about-the-pegasus-project/ (ForbiddenStories)]
**According to the leaked data, NSO Group's Pegasus [[spyware]] was used to target Saudi-American journalist [[Jamal Khashoggi]] and his family and friends in the months before and after [[assassination of Jamal Khashoggi|Khashoggi's killing]]. Khashoggi was assassinated and dismembered in [[Saudi Arabia]]'s embassy in [[Istanbul]] in 2018 by Saudi operatives. NSO previously denied any implication in the killing. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/jul/18/nso-spyware-used-to-target-family-of-jamal-khashoggi-leaked-data-shows-saudis-pegasus (''The Guardian'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[Nashville Predators]] prospect [[Luke Prokop]] [[Coming out|comes out]] as [[gay]], making him the first player in the [[National Hockey League|NHL]] to do so. [https://www.npr.org/2021/07/19/1017915128/luke-prokop-becomes-the-first-nhl-player-under-contract-to-come-out-as-gay (NPR)]
